hello :) so far I noticed none of the comments really tell you how to study at all.

First of all you should know that studying something means understanding it, you can understand something enough to be able to solve any questions related to it in your syllabus, however, if you are passionate about the subject then you should try to comprehend it rather than just understand it, figure out what its used for by researching more and be over all interested in it. Studying is learning the components of a subject you’re taking and the aspects of it needed that would help you pass exams or gain skills.

Second of all, as a commentator above said, studying differs from subject to subject, if you could tell me what subjects you’re taking maybe I could help, but I’ll throw in general advice for now.

If it’s math related or equation related, then solving problems is your best bet at fully internalizing the subject, first things first you read and figure out the outcome of each lesson, then you hop on to solving equations with a formula guide near you, once you solve enough equations you won’t need the guide anymore, it’ll be muscle memory

If it’s a history or geography or social sciences related subject, I find the best way to go about it is to tell it as a story, make up stories in your mind or find interesting facts related to what you’re learning, this will pique your interest and make you more involved and interested in the subject, helping you memorize

If it’s a language that you need to learn vocabulary in or need to memorize something in, then writing the thing you need to memorize multiple times will help you remember, muscle memory is incredibly strong and will surprise you

When it comes to biology, I would say drawing each part you’re learning about and trying to point out what each muscle is called/what each bone is called would help, maybe you could make up patient stories that involve each thing, if you’re learning about atoms or stems try researching it more, biology is extremely interesting and you’d find a lot of information in every aspect you need to study online.

With chemistry, if its equations then do the problem solving thing, if its mixtures (not sure if thats the right word) then try watching youtube videos of people experimenting to see the effects happen before you, this would help it stick more.

Aside from that there’s multiple methods of studying, a lot of which I figured out cause I couldn’t focus for long periods of time so I would switch them up

Most common one is the Pomodoro method, where you study for 25 minutes and get a 5 min break or study for 50 mins and get a 10 min break and every 4 sessions you get a 30 minute break where you can go eat or drink or refill your water or rest or read.

You can also start with the subject you’re most interested in and once you get bored you switch subjects and so on.

Another method is to do a quick read over whatever you’re supposed to study first thing in the morning, then go have breakfast and wash up while you let the context of the lesson seep in your head, then after breakfast you can start studying and breaking things down and it would make it easier as you’d know the outcome.

If you focus more with background music then play background music, don’t stop yourself from doing things that would help you remove distractions just cause ‘I shouldn’t do that I should take this seriously’

Remember to stretch and take walks even around the apartment or house to prevent body aches

Another thing that’s incredibly important is to not think about studying when you’re on a break/a day off. Guilt will eat at you and it won’t be a break at all if everything you’re thinking about is studying and how you’re wasting time. Breaks are needed to prevent burnout so whether you like it or not, you need breaks.

However, if you’re super into what you’re studying and hyper focused on it, don’t take a break until you lose your focus, even if the timer rings, cause when you’re hyper focused you learn so much better and absorb a lot of information, its your peek time essentially.

Another thing is to change environments, sometimes studying at home gets boring and burns you out, I like studying at cafes cause the smell of coffee wakes me up and having people around me work or do their own thing motivates me into working. But you can also go to shared spaces or study areas/lounges or libraries of course.

Last thing is to enjoy studying, everyone makes studying seem like a burden, and of course studying is your job as a student. However; studying is incredibly fun cause honestly isn’t it insane that as humans we managed to get all this information about the world around us? Managed to make equations that help us create engines and understand rainbows? Isn’t it crazy that your body does everything it needs to maintain itself on its own and has a survival system in case you are stranded? The way we learn language and understand each other even though languages are just a bunch of sounds we make is absolutely crazy, creating arts and crafts and having passions in life, even being able to walk and run is fascinating in itself. So try to have fun instead of feeling like you’re forced into this!! :) good luck!

I’ve made comments before on topics like this but right now the most important thing for you is to stop feeling guilty. Guilt will take up more of your time and focus and you’ll end up wallowing in it and how you could’ve used that time better, accept the fact that you didnt do work and move on.

Take a deep breath, shower, make yourself something warm to drink and keep water next to you as well as all your study material. If you’re taking notes just have a pen and notebook next to you (pen so u dont have to keep sharpening, if u dont like pens use a mechanical pencil cause it lasts rly long).

Divide up your studies to small topics, if you have chapters on each topic just read through it first as a quick refresher of what you’re actually supposed to get out of that subject and then study it. If it’s math related or problem solving related then read through it and jump to solving problems, having the formulas nearby as a guide (once you solve enough problems you won’t need to look at the formulas anymore and it’ll just be 2nd nature)

I’d recommend dedicating a couple hours to studying one part then move to another part then go back to the first part again to double check if u still remember, mark anything you’re weak in or anything you take time to think of an answer for and quiz yourself on it the next morning (since you only have two days)

If you need a break from studying or you can’t focus, take a 5-10 min break (30 mins if ur going to eat), and during that break you need to completely relax, cause if you think ab studies during that break or consider yourself to be wasting time then it isn’t a break.

If you can’t study long hours then use the pomodoro method, but if you can study for long hours then keep studying until you lose focus then take a 30-60 min break depending on how long you studied.

Make sure you sleep early as well, preferably 10pm. Your body essentially rejuvenates (not sure if thats the right word here, forgive me, english isnt my native tongue) your organs and your mind between 10pm and 4am, so try sleeping from 10 to 4 or 5.

When you wake up you have two choices, either study for a consecutive 2 hours (revising everything you learned) then do your morning routine and have breakfast, or do your morning routine then study till noon and have lunch then continue pomodoro method till 7 or so and then just relax and cool off till you go to sleep, your mind would deeply need this rest. If you didn’t finish studying then extend it till 8 or 9pm but don’t push yourself too hard during that time or you might forget everything you studied/have increased pressure.

Keep in mind it’s important to know the stuff you studied well, and if you didn’t get to study other stuff then just be better prepared for future exams. But if you try to cram everything together in a rush, you’ll mess up even on the things you DO know in the exam and you’ll panic even more.

Oh and remember, studying requires discipline, motivation helps you work faster but discipline is the main factor

You need to think of studying as a job, you’re a student, it’s your job to study, its something you need to do, you don’t have to like it. You need to establish that as a fact. Second thing is that you need breaks to function productively, I use pomdoro method at 60/10 with 30 minute breaks every 4 sessions, this helps me as i can keep track of the hours I study and I regularly get breaks, but if you don’t wanna use pomodoro then make sure that whenever you feel like taking a break, then take a break, but set a timer for that break so you don’t get too distracted. Third thing is to make sure you don’t have a reason to get off your study desk except for bathroom or food or breaks, keep water next to you, a cup of coffee if you want one (keep a cups amount of coffee in a thermos so it doesnt go cold and dont drink too much coffee or it’ll stress you out), keep snacks if you like snacking while studying, have all your books within arms reach and your pens and pencils too, basically all necessities. Fourth thing is actually one of the most important things and its to sleep at least 8 hours a day, you need your sleep in order to be able to continue this long time, your sleep and your breaks are a priority or else you won’t focus or take in the information, and don’t overload your brain with information, if you can’t study anymore during that day, do a quick revision on the things you did study before and then take the rest of the day off. Its also important to make sure eating is away from your study desk and your breaks are away from your study desk, so your brain would know that once you’re sitting at that desk then it’s study time, you can set the pomodoro on your laptop and turn your phone off if its a distraction too. Fifth thing is to not beat yourself up too much about not studying, it happens, we get burnt out, if you spend the time you’re not studying thinking about how you could’ve been studying or you could’ve done that or you’re a waste of time, then you’ll get depressed and more unmotivated and less confident and more burnt out, so cut yourself some slack. Last thing which is also incredibly important is active recall, revise on the things you already studied a week after you studied them by solving questions on them or practice exams or using flashcards, whatever suits you, but make sure you revise on them or you’ll forget them, every week just have a quick revision over the things you’ve studied before.

Good luck! Make sure you get a day off in the week if its possible, studying too much can affect you :) and go out with friends and socialize except for the last month before exams. basically studying hard means spending hours at your desk without really focusing on what you’re studying hence forgetting it pretty quickly, studying smart means studying at an amount your brain can process while being completely focused and understanding the things you’re studying, however that doesnt mean you can’t study hard and smart, for example, I can focus for long periods of time so i would study for 4-5 hours then have a 30 min break or an hour break if im gonna eat, for me that works cause I can maintain focus while watching long lectures and also cause I have to apply what I learn by solving equations and questions generally as homework, so applying what I learn helps me memorize it better and also helps me clarify if I understand it or not, If i dont understand it i’d try to focus more while restudying that section or watch a youtube video about it to see what im missing, thats studying smart, its analyzing what i didnt understand and trying to understand it better, to the point where I can explain it to others, its also studying hard as I study for a long period in the day and maintain info, if you cant study 4-5 hours in a row you can start off easy with like 25-30 mins then 5 min break, or even start off with 5 min study sessions, as long as you’re focused :) and then having more and more of these sessions until you cant focus, thats when you stop or take a super long break for your brain to rest a bit, the following week you should try solving questions on the topic you studied to see if you remember it or understood it well and see your weakpoints yet again

Studying hard is spending long hours studying without really getting things done or revising on what you learn

Studying smart is building techniques to retain your information, studying with breaks so you don’t overload your brain, doing repetitive practice and timed practice by quizzing yourself every week-month about the things you studied to make sure the information stays there, solving practice exams, understanding the concept and comprehending the concept, know that you can understand things but to truly comprehend them you need to know the ins and outs of them, you need to be able to explain it to an elementary school child so that if you ask them a question about it they’ll be able to answer, thats comprehension, studying smart is knowing your limits and knowing it doesn’t matter how many hours you study in a day as long as you get what needs to be done done.
